stories.title: The man behind Srebrenica: Ratko Mladic dies at 84
stories.summary: For many, Ratko Mladic represented the horrors of the Bosnian War. He was convicted of genocide for the Srebrenica massacre and of other war crimes. Now he has died in detention at The Hague.

Image: Jerry Lampen/REUTERS Advertisement More than 30 years after the end of the war in Bosnia and Herzegovina (1992-1995), Srebrenica remains emblematic of its brutality. And no one is more closely linked to the genocide that took place in the small town in eastern Bosnia than Ratko Mladic , the former commander-in-chief of the Bosnian Serb army. Although the United Nations had declared Srebrenica a "safe area," Bosnian Serb forces attacked the town. Within just a few days in July 1995, they expelled women and children, then killed more than 8,300 unarmed Muslim boys and men in the nearby village of Potocari — on Mladic's direct orders, according to the verdict handed down by the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia (ICTY) in The Hague 22 years later. At the time, Srebrenica was the largest massacre in Europe since World War II . The ICTY classified it as genocide. stories.article_text_excerpt: Skip to content Skip to main menu Skip to more DW sites https://p.dw.com/p/5IlIk One defense method involves interceptor drones, which chase drones and capture them with a net Image: Sina Schuldt/dpa/picture alliance Advertisement On August 25, German media reported on a third drone allegedly found near Leipzig/Halle Airport in August. A drone and a substance — which initial assessments suggest could be around 50 grams of Hexogen, a highly explosive military-grade explosive — were reportedly discovered in a field outside the airport grounds. Consequently, public broadcasters NDR and WDR, and the daily broadsheet Süddeutsche Zeitung are speculating about a plot that may be far more extensive than what has been publicly disclosed so far.
